commit.message: Fix typo in fountain decor line

Fix a crash on demand from pcall when closing the game

When the game has been closed and user defined lua code is still
running, we let the lua code run for a while before killing it by
raising an error. However, there wasn't anything to stop the user
defined lua code from catching the error with pcall and continuing
running which would eventually result in a crash when the server decided
to kill the unresponsive game.

Fix this by setting crawl_state.lua_script_killed to true before raising
the error which lets the pcall function exposed to user lua know to stop
catching errors (the pcall function exposed to user defined lua isn't
the default lua pcall function).

Fix a crash on demand from lua pcall

When running user supplied lua code, we redefined the lua pcall function
to call the c++ _clua_guarded_pcall function. _clua_guarded_pcall would
check if the error message contained
"666: Killing badly-behaved Lua script." and if it did it would throw an
error by calling luaL_error using the error message as the format
string for the new error. This allowed the user to throw an error from
within pcall with format specifiers in it such as
"666: Killing badly-behaved Lua script. %s" which would lead to a crash
when passed into luaL_error as no arguments would be passed to it
matching the format specifiers.

Instead, rethrow all error from _clua_guarded_pcall using lua_error if
crawl_state.lua_script_killed is set.

Fix a crash on demand when loading a lua file

If the user loaded a lua file (such as with loadfile, dofile, or
crawl_require), we would crash if the first byte of the file had the
value 27.

I don't think this lead to any problems in webtiles as I don't think you
can load arbitrary files.

Fix a crash on demand from lua loadstring

The user can call the lua loadstring function from their rc file. We
redefine this function to call our own lua_loadstring c++ function. We
do this as the default lua loadstring function will accept lua bytecode
with basically no validation that the bytecode is valid if the first
byte of the string passed to it has the value 27. Unfortunately, our
replacement function would just call abort if the first byte of the
string passed to it had the value 27 which would let the user crash the
game whenever they wanted to by calling loadstring("\27"). Instead, call
luaL_loadbufferx from our replacement function with mode set to "t" to
force it to treat the string passed to it as lua source code rather than
bytecode no matter the value of its first byte.

fix: crash during serpent of hell breath attack

SoH breaths consecutive spells at once and it would try to cast spells
even if the previous spell resulted in its death. (for instance, by
reflection)

commit.message: Don't show an empty range line on player spells

A new mannequin-deploying shop vault + a few more mannequin tiles

This rare shop vault, split into three individual shops with small
inventory counts, uses talismans, parchments, and occasional equipment
drops to let players cosplay as a monster or other species. To help
clarify this to players and to deploy some of the obscene work done
for Xom in 228b0c0 elsewhere, these vaults display behind glass a
mannequin of whichever monster the shop helps one dress up as, which
should be a cute enough way to connect players and monsters a bit
closer together and justify the mannequin lengths themselves. (It also
contains a variety of build-re/directing options between spells and
talismans without being particularly specific about it). To keep
mannequins fairly special as something built specifically for Xom, this
vault has a low placement weight and stops appearing past V / Elf.

(This commit also comes with a few more mannequin tiles: a mosquito
mannequin tile using roctavian's vampire mosquito tile, as the other
flying insect mannequin option tiles don't particularly fit, and an eel
mannequin further mixing together ontoclasm's adder tile with Denzi's
electric eel tile, to help sell the eel hand mannequin in this shop.)

Make Vexed actors a little less likely to attack empty space

Each real target now has 13 times the weight of empty space, as opposed to
7 times. (This means that with one enemy adjacent, the chance of attacking
it is now 65% instead of 50%. With two, the odds of hitting something is
~81% instead of 70%, etc.)

Make wands of charming Vex the player instead of confuse

This is consistent with Dominate Undead's effect and while Vex is
potentially more dangerous than confusion in general, it is kinder to the
player in certain early situations in particular.

Low XL players tend to have almost no willpower, and monsters use wands
frequently, making it very plausible for early wands of charming to result
in something close to a 'stun lock' situation, where a stumbling player
just gets more and more confused (and this is a point where they mave have
no !curing at all - though even if they did, it mightn't help much). Vex
itself gives protection against being repeatedly affected without a break
and you might even kill the monster with the wand during its effect.

Remove Paralysis from the list of Zot trap effects

The odds of it happening were low, and the odds of it happening while in a
scenario where it might be fatal were lower still, but it's a deeply
dissatisfying way for anyone to die (and not very interesting either, imo,
being generally too rare to be worth paying attention to except that once
in a blue moon you just get clobbered).

Its weight is moved into petrification, which has far more counterplay and
warning.

Tweak Bane of Stumbling's conditions

Internally, Bane of Stumbling used the same criteria as Acrobat,
essentially being an 'anti-acrobat'. But this had a few small wrinkles. For
instance, your EV is lowered on turns you wait in place, but not turns you
*do* anything while standing in place. This had the unfortunate effect of
meaning that you could wait in place without penalty by swinging at the
air. That is silly.

Instead, apply the penalty on any turn the player moves (or is moved by a
spell or external force).

Fix Sif not gifting books until 6*

Even the in-game messages claimed it could happen at 5* (and part of the
intent of simplifying Sif's gifting rate in e86698e was to avoid
discouraging the player from using Exegesis so that they could obtain more
gifts, which is kind of undermined if you need to maintain 6* piety).

(piety_breakpoint() not actually matching visible stars strikes again....)

Increase elementalist ancestor cast rate (by approximately 25%)

While I feel like elementalists have succeeded at being more distinct from
the other options than battlemage were, they are currently underperforming
compared to both other options. Rather than addressing some of their
weaknesses (low HP, noisy), let's first try leaning even harder into their
niche by making them more consistent at the thing they're good at: blasting
monsters.

Make it possible to give parchments of spells with 'of' in their name (r-i)

The 'of' was being stripped out of 'parchment of X' in itemspec, but it was
stripping *all* ofs out, meaning that 'parchment of kiss of death' would
just give you a random spell instead (since 'kiss death' isn't a spell).

Gently nerf Trickster AC

The diminishing returns for stacking increasing amounts of AC is now a bit
stronger (making it take more debuff applications to hit the maximum bonus
for your XL) and it decays faster if you haven't applied any debuffs
recently.

It now also uses fractional AC instead of giving each stack a chance of
applying either 0 or 1 AC.

This also fixes a bug where the decay rate was *inversely* proportional to
how much time passed per turn (ie: it would decay much faster during fast
actions and much slower during slow ones). Poltergeists attacking at 0.5
delay would lose AC at 4 times the rate of ones acting at normal speed (and
'attacking with a trained short blade' being such a common thing for
poltergeists to be doing is why the magnitude of the decay change is as
high as it is - this is still technically slower while doing so)

This shouldn't change any incentives about using debuffs as a poltergeist
(which I think are good), but just gently reduce their overall power (which
is quite high).

Nerf Mark of the Celebrant

This has been absolutely dominating the winrate stats for Makhleb marks for
some time now (even after previously being nerfed). This commit mildly
reduces its damage (moreso at low Invocations), but also makes the
threshold for firing 1/3rd of max HP instead of 50%. This should further
reinforce its identity as 'help when in real danger' rather than often
ending situations *before* they become too uncomfortable. (It probably also
reduces the chance to quickly reset its own cooldown by healing you back to
full.)

This probably isn't enough to dethrone it from 1st place, but we'll see in
the fullness of time.

Significantly adjust Potion of Experience formula

Potions of experience worked by, essentially, giving the player skill xp
equal to 750 * their current XL. This ignored the cost of skill points
entirely, resulting in giving an obscene amount of skill at low XL and a
almost totally irrelevant amount of skill at high XL.

In fact, it was so obscene that, for instance, quaffing at XL 1 gave XP as
if the player had gone from XL 1 to XL ~10.8!. (But by XL 21, would give
less than 25% of the XP required to reach the next XL).

It also had a couple other odd effects. By giving huge amounts of
'experience' directly, it automatically increased the cost of all future
skill points (so the player would get an outrageous skill boost, but then
have their training enormously slowed down for a while, like they had
borrowed from their own future). Also, since skill point cost ignores XP
apt, but the amount of XP given by the potion does not, species with bad
XP apts would get meaningfully less out of an experience potion than those
with good ones.

This commit changes the potions to work closer to giving skill point
directly, accounting for current skill point cost. It still gives more
skill points when quaffed at high levels, to account for the fact that an
equivalent amount of skill points are worth much less then (since so many
relevant skills are already highly trained). The XP given by them is also
now 'free' and will not slow down future training.

In effect, !xp should have a considerably smaller immediate effect at low
XL (though not borrow from their future), while being much more impactful
at high XL. (Very approximately something like 1/3rd as good at XL 4 as
before, but 5.5 times as good at XL 21.)

This *does* mean there is a modest incentive to wait a little before
quaffing the potion, as it will actually do more if you hold off. But I
think that might create an interesting tension between "Immediate power is
better than delayed power" and "But the delayed power is actually larger.",
depending on how well the player is doing in the short-term.
Add another adjective to gizmos.

Tweak quotes.txt

Mostly this involves cutting inappropriate quotes- sky beasts no longer
turn invisible or attack with electricity as of f9d8110, the cloak of the
Thief doesn't generate any fog clouds as of 4936369, and so on and so
forth.

Fix up + update ploomutoo_gammafunk_necropolis_ghost_potion_laboratory

While 6d75ccc had presumed that most mutagenic fog vaults were mostly
ugly thing based that thus could survive the change to use flux-form style
contamination instead, the titular Necropolis ghost subvault was fairly
mixed together and directly placed a variety of non-ugly-thing monsters
directly by item rewards, allowing shouting and then running away to
slowly kill everything in the vault via contamination explosions. It also
tried to place a lot more monsters than it could actually fit in its
sections, and also didn't really risk almost any contamination if one
already knew Apportation.

This commit heavily changes the vault to make it work with the new
mutagenic fog behaviour:

 * Mutagenic cloud distribution is fixed instead of randomized and
   made fairly larger, so it's actually tangibly noticeble to try
   and walk past it.

 * The first section now only contains ugly things or very ugly things,
   so the previous shapeshifters no longer slowly explode over time.
   (This does also mean no longer placing the vault in Vaults or Elf,
   as normal ugly things do not show up in either of these branches.)

 * There are now three sets of transporters in an expanded three discrete
   sections, making it much harder to lure the player ghost and its
   mutated allies into the earlier mutagenic fog plus seperating the
   item rewards + mutagenic fog mechanics into its own third section.

 * The player ghost's company tries to match the originally intended
   large selection of monsters with mild nerfs, effectively slightly
   reducing threats in the D:8-11 version, mildly increased in the
   D:12-15 version, and wildly buffed in the Depths section (though
   players are plenty strong and the item rewards were fairly good
   at such a point).

I'd like to keep an eye on this fairly different iteration of the
vault, whether or not the clouds feel annoying to time walking through
or the new transporter threat levels make the item rewards not quite
feel worth it, but this should help heavily fix up the vault for now.

Hide friendly + behind-glass slime creature merge animations

The animation for slime creatures changing from a flash to a ring in
cfa9558 was a good step forward, but the animation is still fairly
obnoxious in the case of allied slime creatures (who can merge and unmerge
multiples while just resting, and which are slightly more common than
previously with boggart Xom guardians in b5223ba) and slime creatures
stuck behind glass (which can be seen in e.g. serial_aquarium or a
few runed door vaults). As such, this commit removes the ring animation
(but not the flash_tile piece) for either case, which still should be
noticeable for runed door purposes but hopefully not be nearly as
obnoxious to sit through.

Add some guardian mannequins to Xom bazaars

The extreme tile lengths done for mannequins in 228b0c0 means that I'd
like to keep an eye on any additional plausible placements for them, and
associating them with shops is a reasonable flavour connection to fit them
in with. Xom bazaars have gotten a touch more threat to them in this push
as a candidate level for the reinforcements of 0279637, though it
otherwise is not much of a significant nerf to Xom threat to reduce the
capacity to be killed in Their bazaars versus almost anywhere else, so I
have thus fit in six good_neutral guardian mannequins- vault, serpent,
crystal, or sphinx at random- patrolling the very entrance of the bazaar.
(As with general bazaar costumers, they will disappear if you've
Sacrificed Love and joined Xom, for whatever single-digit number of games
have done this.)

Add another two simulacrum tiles

While we're still a very long ways off from having a reasonably accurate
simulacrum list, these two quick adjustments of extant tiles should
help with both flight tracking and noticing one particularly dangerous
simulacrum type in guardian sphinxes (multiple hits, high HD, not slow).
This commit adds both a iron dragon simulcrum (modified from ontoclasm's
dragon simulacrum tile) and a winged quadruped tile for manticores and
sphinxes (mixing ontoclasm's drake, large quadruped, and large humanoid
simulacrum tiles).

Adjust Xom summons / guardians further

 * When the initial custom Xom summons list was made back in db1107a,
   chaos spawn were naturally weighted fairly highly and appeared for
   a fairly long level range to get more chaos threats to endanger or
   support Xom worshippers. With chaos brand being fairly more common
   both ways than prior (with the many options of the Xom Bazaar plus
   battleshapes in bd39355 and reinforcements in 0279637), and with
   blessing guardians now wanting higher total Xom monster variety,
   chaos spawns don't need to be nearly as common as prior. As such,
   this commit cuts their weight by 33% and lowers their XL range
   (give or take Xom's high variance) from XL 18 to XL 15.

 * Some of the very highest rolls have been tweaked a bit when rolling
   for extra-high experience levels with more than three runes, reducing
   the support monster presence of moths of wrath and apocalypse crabs
   for very slightly more nekomata, as most characters and enemies can
   easily kill the support monsters by the time one is dipping into
   extended.

 * Shapeshifters as guardian allies, while cute for raw variety, are also
   very awkward in practice: their transformations both interrupt regular
   exploration and can be gamed with stairs to try and get a good
   shapeshifted monster roll. As such, both regular shapeshifters and
   glowing shapeshifters are now banned from guardians.

 * The Xom guardian roll itself has a fairly high amount of variance
   with the way it calls on extant summon code: it calls for a single
   ally with the selection used for many summons at once, giving it
   an effective roll of one's XL to one's XL minus 3 below XL 19. With
   the way Crawl's power curve works in earlygame and midgame, and with
   with Xom's summon list already emphasizing a large number of support
   monsters a bit beyond their otherwise effective danger range, this has
   a fairly dissatisfying amount of variance that can e.g. pull up tier-5
   demons in Lair or tier-4 demons in Lair branches. (Additionally,
   it can provide Zot, Pan, or Zig themed guardians in those locations
   but not anywhere else, which is weird for a god effect.)

   This commit thus tweaks guardian picking code in multiple ways:

   * The effective XL range has shifted to always be just one's XL plus
     or minus one, which can pull stronger guardians but still has a
     large number of mediocre rolls for that XL (instead of completely
     outclassed ones).

   * Through some quick code rearranging, there is now a very low chance
     to roll various Zot / Pan / Zig enemies (klowns, progenitors, death
     cobs, toes, demonspawn blood saints and corrupters, pan lords, player
     ghosts) at XL 27 regardless of the branch one is in, with that chance
     improving slowly over getting more than 3 runes.

   While this is a notable buff fairly shortly after Xom's blessing
   system was added just this version, the lategame relative frailty of
   a monster one can't immediately resummon already places a lot of caps
   on the total effectiveness of later guardians, and it'll be much
   easier to assess any intent or desire of power when it doesn't give
   ufetubi to XL 11 characters in Lair.
Fix spelling.
Fix typo.
Fix a typo (Darby)

Make Xom-made mannequins worship Xom

For better messaging when priestly mannequins use invocations.

Make trample attacks a little less spammy while wearing Mountain Boots

There's already a message for resisting trample, which always got printed
*on top of* the boots saying that you resisted being trampled. This is
probably a touch excessive.

Make Fortress Blast prevent you from being dislodged while channelling

Rather than have the spell get easily interrupted by trampling/dragging,
make the spell itself prevent such things. Feels thematically appropriate
and ocassionally useful on its own (and the spell isn't exactly wildly
popular at present, so I assume it will handle this buff just fine).

Since it's hooked into the same code as Mountain Boots, it can also
*technically* prevent you from being shafted, though whoever manages to
ever witness this happening deserves a cookie.

Allow mountain dwarves to use ?brand weapon on randarts

While their artefact enchanting perk is fun in theory, in many games you
can already use all the ?ea scrolls you find just enchanting up the heavy
body armour they are undoubtedly already using and may not have almost any
use for them to use on randart aux armour.

This should be minorly more exciting and a way of further customizing some
of the artefact gear they find.

Reduce mistmane mist potion distillation rate

While the form wasn't necessarily overpowered as a whole, the rate at which
it generated mist potions was effectively high enough that ammo management
regarding them was somewhat sidelined. This should make them a *bit* more
limited.

(Also, this fixes a bug where the stated increase to distillation rate
listed on the talisman properties table just didn't... actually do
anything.)

It should take about 90% longer to generate a potion at 8 skill than it
currently does and 25% longer at 14.

Properly end Disguised status on performing a ranged attack

This fixes #5565

Fix chaotic unrand armour not getting its chaos property until reloading

Since it was handled in setup_unrandart() (to avoid it being *overwritten*
on reload) and the item isn't actually given the chaotic flag until after
that. This resulted in it not getting it at all, until the save is
reloaded. Now, also add it manually, too.

Don't anger allies by casting Lesser Beckoning on them (Ogregutan)

Or even penance!

It doesn't feel like an intrinsically harmful actions (and allies in
general don't mind being displaced by most non-damaging translocations).

I have some minor concerns about it encouraging micromanagement of allies,
but it seems unclear it would be any different/worse than what one can
already do by shouting orders.

Make Passwall give fractional AC instead of randomly rounded AC per cast

This makes very little practical difference, but is slightly cleaner
internally and makes the spell UI marginally clearer.

Don't automatically break fear when recalling Apostles (Acrobat)

Yet another wrinkle of fear being partially an enchant and partially a
behaviour type....
Capitalise skill names when Ash offers you knowledge (Ge0ff)

Fix Enfeeble's listed success chance ignoring Orb of Guile

The spell itself would benefit from it, but the UI would not indicate this.

Make becomming frenzied interrupt monster Word of Recall (Flugkiller)

(And other channelled spells.)

Fix jademantle crystals having overly high HP at extremely low skill

If the player's shapeshifting was below 2, the expected HP of a jade
crystal would round down to 0 and instead give them the 'default' HP for
their type (which was ~140, otherwise taking somewhat over 8 skill).

Instead, just cap their HP at 1.

(Even gargoyle mystics start with more skill than this, so it only affects
non-mystics finding the talisman.)

Fix a message when vexed monsters attack unseen tiles

It would print a message like "The vault guard attacks !"
Fix randart vision talismans getting SInv (predelnik)

Prevent polymorphing orb guardians

Polymorphing an orb guardian before killing them allows one to get around
the tesseract activating from killing them. I think doing this
comprehensively *usually* isn't plausible given their willpower, but
sometimes is.

I've been on the fence about doing anything about this for a while now, but
settled on this solution over either starting tesseracts upon the death of
whatever they polymorphed into (sometimes confusing and unexpected) or upon
first being polymorphed (unexpected in a different way and possible to
happen without direct player action). This change feels the cleanest to me.

Don't activate tesseracts if orb guardians die without player involvement

In very rare scenarios, an orb guardian could die to the environment
without the player having ever ever seen them (one of the more plausible
scenarios involves miasma trails from curse toes, though even this seems
rare enough that multiple curse toes might need to be involved).

Instead, if an orb guardian dies with 0 friendly damage being dealt to them
(ie: *entirely* without involvement of anything that would give the player
XP), don't activate the alarm.

I have tried to consider scenarios where the player could exploit this, but
most of them seem unhelpful (for instance, using your own face to convince
orbs of fire to kill them as collatoral). Jiyva jellies seem unlikely to
kill even one guardian before the Zot clock happens. Hopefully I'm not
overlooking anything with actual impact.

Tweak Vainglory's description

To try and make it slightly more clear that the effect happens *any* time
you enter a different floor, not just the first time.

Replace gnoll's shapeshifter recommendation with mystic

They are probably much more outstanding mystics than they are
shapeshifters, so this feels like a more appropriate metamorph
recommendation to me.

Properly prevent orb run spawns from appearing in Oka's arena (Flugkiller)

I attempted to fix this in 87d53ae but the fix was in the wrong place. This
should *actually* work this time.

Mark plasmodia and assassin centipedes as no_poly_to

The former were sometimes (somewhat bafflingly) showing up in V:5
(presumably as a result of a shapeshifter turning into a rock fish and
then transforming again while in a wall), and the latter are a bit overly
vanilla as enemies in their default stats.

Make rPois- only cause the player to take +50% poison instead of +100%

Direct poison damage was only increased by 50% from rPois- (as it is with
essentially all negative resists), but the amount of poison DoT applied to
the player was doubled. Making this also +50% feels more consistent.

(This is effectively a buff to a couple of talisman forms and a nerf to
naga ritualists, but that seems okay - several of those forms are less
popular, in part *because* of the rPois-, and ritualists are doing quite
well for themselves and will only be affected in cases where an rPois0
player also gets hit by Virulence, in which case they're probably still
having a bad time.)

Make malmutation drain undead players a little more

It's fine to be more resiliant against mutations, but the cost felt a
little *too* cheap to me.

Tweak Gozag wrath

Remove the chance to block potion usage (which was always phrased extremely
weirdly - who is *Gozag* petitioning for this to happen?) and instead
deduct half of the player's gold upon abandonment, as a cancellation fee.

Also, make Gozag's incite effect able to give brilliance to spellcasting
monsters instead of just haste.

Rename Potion Petition to Purchase Blessing

The fact that potion petition doesn't work like drinking a real potion is a
constant source of confusion for newcomers. They can be used by mummies,
their healing works on vine stalkers, they don't cause oni to attack nearby
monsters, they can't produce clouds with mistmane, they don't interact with
Kyrias - the list goes on and on!

Them *not* being subject to those limitations is fairly important (for
mummies in particular), so after some discussion, it was agreed that it
might be better to just call this something else and attempt to remove the
potion association entirely.

This also opens the door to future non-potion-based effects from this
ability, those this commit does not add any itself.

---------------------------

The new Purchase Blessing icon and vfx were made by regret-index, with the
icon using a CC0 bag of gold by ArlanTR, and the vfx combining ontoclasm's
Bribe Branch icon with the previous CC0 vfx by codemanu.

She needs the same fix as the poly'd Lernaean hydra corpse.

The other monsters that have MB_NAME_THE (the Royal Jelly and all
variants of the Serpent of Hell) don't leave corpses, so this fix

(Xom can polymorph all of them even if the player can't.)

Use "maniacally laughing," to better follow the pattern of e.g.

Fix error in S_SHOUT2 speaking message.

Adjust default shout in do_mon_str_replacements()

Make it NUM_SHOUTS instead of -1, since both produce the same result,
and this should make it easier to eventually make the function use a
shout_type instead of an int, since the shout_type has no entry at -1.

Put shouting checks in the same order.

First S_SILENT, then NUM_SHOUTS, then NUM_LOUDNESS.

Add __BUGGY lines for monster verbs.

They still should never be displayed, but let's cover them just in case.

Update shouting-related comment.

Now that there are multiple functions that return __BUGGY for missing
shout types.
Fix missing %%%% in monster croak verb entry.
Add another Xom reaching message.
Add more bland names.

Move monster speech verbs to the database.

Now, when adding a new shout type, all text related to it should be in
the database.

Reorder a few shout entries.

So that the unseen entry comes before the seen entry in all cases,
and so that all entries are in the same order as their shout types.
Add another name to artefact spellbooks.
Add another colour to the database.
Fix a typo (not_that_greg)
Replace a few duplicated names.
Add more bland names.

Expand Xom guardian names a bit.

Now you can get e.g. Bob, Not-Bob, and Not-Not-Bob in addition to e.g.
Bob, Other Bob, and Other Other Bob.
Fix typo.

Reorganize monster speaking-related verbs.

Move the one list of speaking-related verbs from an array in
mon-util.cc:do_mon_str_replacements() (with unused whispering-related
bits) and the other list of speaking-related verbs from a map in
xom.cc to two maps in shout.cc after the keys map there, all accessible
via functions.

This way, whenever a new shout type is added, all shouting-related keys
and verbs are all in the same source file one after the other, instead
of in three different source files.
Simplify Xom check for voiceless word of recall.

fix(tutorial): depluralize some tutorial messages

So that it's possible to learn Mephitic Cloud when the tutorial

Also, handle cawing and laughing in Xom speech keys.

Fix a crash with low level eisegesis blessings

Eisegesis could roll spell level two, but has no level two spells in the
list, which causes a crash. I'm not 100% sure of the intent here, but
this will stop the crashes.

Make casting Yara's cause contam

In lieu of reducing its utility by moving the anti-summon part back out to
another spell (for which a satisfactory design hasn't developed), cause
some contamination on cast, about 90% as much as for irradiate. Might
require a little more thought about when to use it, but the spell retains

Make Valour beams from Xom's cleave(valour) blessing do damage if unarmed

They were being calculated as if the weapon's base damage was 0, resulting
in 4d0 damage being dealt.

Fix Xom guardians sometimes getting lost in the Abyss

Guardians are meant to automatically transit with the player when they
leave any floor, but the Abyss only places transiting monsters 50% of the
time. So things like Xom's fake banishment could pull them in the Abyss,
but fail to place them there when the player arrived, meaning that when the
player left again, they wouldn't come with them. And since they didn't DIE,
their respawn wouldn't be scheduled.

In fact, if you lost a guardian this way, you could still run into it again
later after a pseudobanishment, even if you had been given a different
guardian by that point!

(Looking at the code, I *think* this flag should prevent the Abyss from
failing to place them, avoiding this problem.)
